<div align="center">

# Pull Request

</div>

## Summary

What changed, and what it means for someone holding a cubin.

## Type of change

- [ ] feat (new capability)
- [ ] fix (defect)
- [ ] docs (documentation only)
- [ ] perf (performance)
- [ ] refactor / chore (no behaviour change)

## Area (select all that apply)

- [ ] ISA derivation (`harvest/`, `isa/`, `probe/`)
- [ ] Checker (`verify/`)
- [ ] Scheduler (`sched/`)
- [ ] Assembler (`asm/`)
- [ ] Hardware measurement (`gpu/`)
- [ ] Controls and reproducibility (`scripts/`)
- [ ] Documentation

## Linked issues

Closes #<id> (or) Related to #<id>

## Evidence

The bar in this repository is that a claim names the command that produces it.
Paste the output, not a description of it.

```text
# e.g. python scripts/assembler_coverage.py --opt 3
```

- [ ] The vendor compiler still agrees. Nothing here makes basalt flag `ptxas`
      output that `ptxas` itself scheduled
- [ ] Any number this changes in the README, `docs/FINDINGS.md` or
      `docs/METHOD.md` has been recomputed, not adjusted by hand
- [ ] A new constant is mined or measured, or is documented as an assumption
      with the reason it could not be

## Checklist

### Code quality
- [ ] `ruff check .` and `ruff format --check .` pass
- [ ] `mypy --platform linux` and `mypy --platform win32` both pass
- [ ] Comments explain the non-obvious "why" and nothing else

### Testing
- [ ] `pytest -m "not toolchain and not gpu and not slow"` passes
- [ ] Toolchain-marked tests run if this touches decoding, assembly or the ISA
- [ ] GPU-marked runs reported below if this touches latency or the hazard model,
      naming the card

### Scope
- [ ] No NVIDIA source, headers or decompiled output ([NOTICE](../NOTICE))
- [ ] No claim of support for an architecture nothing was measured on
- [ ] Generated data under `data/` was regenerated by its script, not edited

## Risks

What breaks if this is wrong, and how it would show up.
